hook: Every graph you met last week is about to MOVE — same shape, new address.
objective: Students will describe and apply vertical and horizontal shifts of the parent functions, and state the domain and range of the shifted graph.
bellRinger: Sketch $y=x^{2}$ and $y=|x|$ from memory. Label each vertex/corner. (60 seconds — no calculator.)
agenda: Bell ringer (5) · Go over (5) · Launch: shifts (12) · Video (6) · Guided notes (8) · Worksheet start (9) · Exit ticket (3)
assessment: Exit ticket: describe every shift of a translated reciprocal function and give its domain and range.

long.title: Graphing translations of parent functions — Mathispower4u

questions: Which part of the equation moved the graph sideways — inside or outside the function?
Why does $f(x-3)$ move RIGHT even though it says minus?
What happens to the domain and range when a graph slides?

videoPlacement: After the launch deck, before guided notes — it re-explains the inside/outside rule in a second voice.

script.title: Bell ringer
script.do: Post the two parent sketches task; circulate and spot who still confuses x² and |x|.
options: Have two students sketch on the board while others work
script.say: Where does the vertex of each one live?

script.title: Go over bellwork
script.do: Fix the two sketches on the board; mark (0,0) on both.
options: Cold-call for domain and range of each parent
script.say: Both live at the origin — keep that picture; today we make them MOVE.

script.title: Launch deck — shifts
script.do: Run the launch presentation: hook, the two shift rules, vocab, worked example, the inside-sign trap, you-try.
options: Have students chorally answer the you-try before revealing
script.say: Inside the function lies to you — outside tells the truth.

script.title: Video
script.do: Play the short video; students answer the 3 video questions on their bell-ringer sheet.
options: Skip if the deck ran long; assign the long video as reinforcement
script.say: Watch for WHY the minus sign moves it right.

script.title: Guided notes
script.do: Fill the notes together: formula bank, both examples, students try the You-Trys solo.
options: Pair the You-Trys: partner A describes, partner B writes the equation
script.say: Say the move out loud before you write it.

script.title: Worksheet
script.do: Start the worksheet; Types 1-2 solo, Type 3 with a partner if needed.
options: Early finishers take the Challenge point-tracking problem
script.say: Restrictions and ranges move WITH the graph.

script.title: Exit ticket
script.do: Collect the reciprocal-shift exit ticket at the door.
script.say: Name the moves, then the domain and range.

notes:
## Shifting Parent Functions
A **translation** slides a graph without changing its shape.
- **Outside** the function: $f(x)+k$ moves UP $k$; $f(x)-k$ moves DOWN $k$ (as written).
- **Inside** the function: $f(x-h)$ moves RIGHT $h$; $f(x+h)$ moves LEFT $h$ (opposite!).

**Worked:** $y=\sqrt{x-2}+3$ → right 2, up 3; the start point $(0,0)$ lands at $(2,3)$; domain $x\ge 2$, range $y\ge 3$.

**You try:** describe $y=x^{3}+5$, then write the equation for $|x|$ shifted right 3.

vocab.def: any change made to a {{parent function|3.2cm}}'s graph
a {{slide|2cm}} — the shape and size stay exactly the same

examples.label: Type 1 — describe the shift
examples.prompt: Describe every shift of $y=\sqrt{x-2}+3$ and name the new start point.
steps: Inside: $x-2$ moves the graph {{right 2|2.4cm}} (inside is opposite).
Outside: $+3$ moves it {{up 3|2cm}} (outside is as written).

examples.label: Type 2 — write the equation
examples.prompt: Write the equation: $y=|x|$ shifted left 4 and down 1.
steps: Left 4 goes INSIDE with the opposite sign: $|x$ {{$+4$|1.6cm}}$|$.

examples.label: Type 3 — domain & range after the shift
examples.prompt: State the domain and range of $y=\sqrt{x-2}+3$.
steps: The graph starts at $(2,3)$ and runs right and up, so the domain is $x\ge$ {{$2$|1.4cm}}.
The lowest output is the start height: range $y\ge$ {{$3$|1.4cm}}.

youTry.answer: Up 5 only; the center point moves to $(0,5)$.

youTry.prompt: Write the equation: $y=\sqrt{x}$ shifted right 6 and down 2, then give its domain and range.

guidedNotes.summary: Inside the function moves {{opposite|2.6cm}}; outside moves {{as written|2.8cm}}. The domain and range {{slide with the graph|3.6cm}}.

vocab.definition: any change to a parent function's graph
a slide — same shape, new location

slides.heading: Same U, new address
bullets: One of them just... moved. Where did it go, and what in the equation moved it?
By the end of class you'll slide ANY parent anywhere on the grid.
slides.graphCaption: y = x² (indigo) and its twin (gold) — same shape, new address

slides.heading: The two shift rules
bullets: **Outside** the function → vertical, **as written**: $f(x)+k$ up, $f(x)-k$ down.
The shape never changes — only the address.
slides.graphCaption: y = √x slid left 5, up 2 — the start point carries the whole graph

vocab.definition: any change to a parent's graph
a slide — shape and size unchanged

slides.heading: We do:  y = √(x − 2) + 3
slides.example:
**1.** Inside: $x-2$ → RIGHT 2 (inside is opposite).
**2.** Outside: $+3$ → UP 3 (outside is as written).
**3.** Start point: $(0,0)\to(2,3)$.
**4.** Domain $x\ge 2$; range $y\ge 3$ — they slide with the graph.

slides.heading: The inside sign lies
slides.mistake:
$y=(x-3)^{2}$ moves **RIGHT** 3 — not left.
The inside asks "what $x$ makes this zero?" $x=3$ does, so the vertex now lives at $x=3$.
slides.note: Read the inside as: the value that makes it zero is the new home.

slides.heading: Your turn
slides.youTry:
(a) Describe every shift: $y=x^{3}+5$
(b) Write the equation: $y=|x|$ shifted right 3

bullets: **Wed** — combine moves + write equations from a graph.
**Thu** — graph any transformed parent from scratch.

procedureExamples.prompt: Write the equation: $y=\dfrac{1}{x}$ shifted right 4 and down 3.
State the domain and range of $y=\dfrac{1}{x-4}-3$.
steps: The vertical asymptote moves to $x=4$: domain $x\neq 4$.
The horizontal asymptote moves to $y=-3$: range $y\neq -3$.

worksheet.title: Shifting the Parent Functions
worksheet.instructions: Use the two shift rules: outside moves as written, inside moves opposite. Domains and ranges slide with the graph.

sections.workedExample: **Example:** $y=(x-3)^{2}+2$ — inside $x-3$ moves RIGHT 3, outside $+2$ moves UP 2. The vertex lands at $(3,2)$.
sections.directions: Name the parent, then describe every shift.

sections.why: Reverse the rules: the described move tells you exactly what to write inside (opposite) and outside (as written).
sections.directions: Write the equation for each described shift.

sections.type: Domain and range after the shift
sections.why: The domain and range slide exactly as far as the graph does.
sections.directions: State the domain AND range of each shifted function.

procedure: Find the inside move (opposite of the sign) and the outside move (as written).
Track ONE key point — vertex, corner, or start point.
Slide the domain and range with the graph.
For reciprocal graphs, slide both asymptotes.
optionalExtra: 🌶 The point $(1,1)$ sits on $y=\sqrt{x}$. Exactly where does it land on $y=\sqrt{x+5}+2$? Explain both moves.

extension.title: Challenge
extension.prompt: Pick ANY parent function and write an equation that lands its key point (vertex, corner, or start) exactly at $(4,-1)$. Prove it by naming the two moves.
extension.why: applying both shift rules in reverse

exitTicket: Describe every shift of $y=\dfrac{1}{x+5}-2$, then give its domain and range.

answerKey.section: Domain and range after the shift

answers: $(1,1)\to(-4,3)$: inside $x+5$ slides left 5 ($1\to-4$), outside $+2$ slides up 2 ($1\to3$)
